title: 实现 Core 事务 outbox 发布器与事件恢复切片
objective: 以有界切片完成 Core 固定顺序第 7 步的 outbox 发布与事件恢复（W06）：把既有各写入方在同一事务追加的 INTERNAL/PENDING outbox 记录按已锁定事件契约原子转换为 PUBLISHED，支持可重投（at-least-once）、进程崩溃后的恢复与卡滞/失败记录的显式告警暴露；用按 event_id 幂等的测试消费者验证重投下业务不重复。无真实消费者前不做跨服务网络投递，不引入新的外部消息系统运行依赖，readiness 约束不变。
in_scope: Core outbox 模块：发布器应用端口与实现，PENDING 到 PUBLISHED 的单事务状态转换、publishedAt 回填、并发防双投（数据库行锁或等价原子条件更新，进程内假设不算约束）
可重投：失败重试上限与退避、失败与卡滞记录的显式暴露（计数/结构化指标面），同批可安全重跑
事件恢复：进程重启后从 PENDING 无丢失继续，发布崩溃在状态转换提交前不产生半发布状态；恢复演练有自动化证据
幂等消费者验证夹具：按 event_id 去重的测试消费者证明 at-least-once 重投下不重复处理
发布前按锁定事件 Schema（0.1.0-alpha.4 的 credit.changed.v1 与 event-envelope）校验内部载荷；不修改锁定文件
既有写入方（identity、developer-app、token-metadata、entitlement、credits）同事务审计与 INTERNAL outbox 行为回归保持
按开发计划第 7 步补齐指标/追踪的可观测验收（基于既有 OpenTelemetry 基线，只读暴露）
更新 Core STATUS、开发计划、acceptance 与 runtime 文档；Contracts 仅在实现证据要求时按实际需要另行声明为辅助（预计无公共契约变化）
out_of_scope: 任何真实跨服务网络投递、Kafka/RabbitMQ 等新中间件、Redis/worker 新运行依赖（readiness 不变）
奖励数值、兑换价格与公共积分消费/退款 HTTP 表面（W05，等 Q-003/Q-013）
Developer App Keycloak OIDC 客户端生命周期（W03，按框架在 Core 锁上排在 W06 之后）
修改 Contracts 锁定文件、Community/Skin/Ops 业务文件或 Skin 工作流（SKIN-008 blocked 锁保持原样）
生产部署、镜像公开发布、消费者产品集成
contract_impact: none expected: the credit.changed.v1 envelope and EventEnvelope schemas are already locked at 0.1.0-alpha.4 (lock commit 9a85b98); the publisher validates internal payloads against those locked files read-only and no public API, scope, error code, event or schema changes
acceptance_evidence: Core format、lint、严格 typecheck、单元、隔离 PostgreSQL 集成、HTTP E2E、architecture、migration、契约与 build 全部通过，最终 runtime 镜像从最终提交源码重建并冒烟（非 root、迁移、live/ready）
并发双发布器对同一批 PENDING 记录只产生一次 PUBLISHED 转换，其余安全重试；失败记录在重试上限内可重投，超限显式暴露
发布进程在转换前崩溃后重启不丢记录、不产生半发布状态；恢复演练自动化
按 event_id 幂等的测试消费者在人工重投下不重复处理同一事件
载荷按锁定 Schema 校验通过；非法载荷被拒绝并暴露，不标记 PUBLISHED
既有 identity/developer-app/token-metadata/entitlement/credits 同事务审计与 outbox 写入回归全绿
指标/告警面：PENDING 积压、失败与卡滞计数可观测并有测试
validation_results: Preflight verified 2026-10-05 ~23:40 (Codely/Mac): authoritative W06 definition read from the owner framework (audit/outbox/event-recovery; acceptance themes atomic records, re-deliverable publishing, idempotent consumers, alerting); entry gates CORE-005 closed plus locked event protocol at alpha.4 are satisfied; live registry = 29 completed with only SKIN-008 (blocked, Skin-only) active after FOUNDATION-009 closed W01 minutes earlier; Foundation back on clean main (4 final unpushed closure commits ride this registration push); Core main 5508d60 and Contracts main e434d93 (pushed to origin under owner authorization 23:34) both clean; MCP-F1-CORE-006 is the next unused Core ID and the Session-1 draft that predicted CORE-006 for the dev-app Keycloak slice is explicitly not a reservation (that slice is W03 and serializes after W06 on the Core lock); W06 registers Core-only per the framework preamble that auxiliaries are declared only when actually needed

Owner transport ruling recorded (2026-10-05 ~23:45, in-chat decision on the W06 blocker flagged by another session): the bounded mechanics slice proceeds WITHOUT binding any production delivery transport; the production default binds no sink, so no record is ever marked PUBLISHED on a stand-in and the at-least-once guarantee is preserved for real future consumers; the transport ADR (broker vs HTTP-push vs consumer-pull) plus a Contracts delivery-semantics lock remain the explicit prerequisites for the future real-delivery/consumer slice, and this slice changes no public contract

Core implementation checkpoint bf1d5695f8b37a0e6811fd9044b467ea6e8935e4: outbox module with application ports (OutboxSink pluggable delivery adapter, OutboxMetrics, OutboxStore), a structural envelope payload gate that mirrors only the locked envelope field names (contract test proves lockstep with the actual locked credit.changed.v1 + event-envelope schemas), and OutboxPublisherService claiming a bounded batch, validating, delivering and only then flipping PENDING to PUBLISHED with publishedAt — a crash before that commit simply leaves the record retryable, so no half-published state exists; PrismaOutboxStore claims with a single UPDATE over a FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED subquery with attempt-count and backoff eligibility, marks with a conditional state guard and records truncated last_error failures; OTel drain counters plus a retryable/waiting/stuck backlog gauge and an interval runner with overlap guard; the module binds OUTBOX_SINK to null by owner decision; sixth forward-only migration adds attempt_count/last_attempt_at/last_error to outbox_records; new OUTBOX_* configuration keys with safe defaults, .env.example and test-config updated

Core gates passed at bf1d569: format:check, lint with zero warnings, strict typecheck, unit 80/80 (6 new publisher tests: no-sink idle never claims and still reports backlog, deliver-and-mark, sink-failure and invalid-payload paths without publishing, already-published race counted, long error truncation), HTTP E2E 57/57, architecture for 71 source files, migration:validate for 6 forward-only migrations, build, and contract 17/17 (6 new: the structural gate accepts a real locked-schema envelope and rejects missing event_id/type/data/producer in lockstep with the locked AJV-compiled schemas); real PostgreSQL integration 39/39 with 8 new outbox tests: full-batch drain sets PUBLISHED with publishedAt and attempt bookkeeping; a concurrent dual drain converges over rounds with exactly-once delivery per record under SKIP LOCKED plus backoff exclusion of in-flight rows, including the documented PostgreSQL behavior that SKIP LOCKED applies after LIMIT so a concurrent round may starve rows which the next cycle recovers; a crash between delivery and the PUBLISHED commit redelivers and the event_id-deduplicating test consumer processes the duplicate exactly once (at-least-once proof); a claim whose process crashed before publishing is recovered on the next drain; an invalid envelope payload is rejected, never published and exposed as stuck after the attempt cap with the backlog gauge; the retry backoff window holds failed records as waiting until it passes; the existing credits and entitlement in-transaction writers keep producing valid PENDING records that drain publishes; and the wired application lifecycle drains automatically on a 250ms interval with the recording sink
